schema: cudaq-pulse reference values v0 (analytic, first-principles and paper-sourced only)

conventions.units: time ns, angular rates rad/ns, frequencies Hz unless *_MHz/*_GHz
conventions.frame: one rotating frame per qudit at its bare 0-1 frequency (cudaq-pulse convention)
conventions.drive: H_d = (A/2)(E a^dag + E^* a), E = envelope * exp(-i (w_tone - w_q) t + i phi) [physical sign]; amplitude_scale_rad_per_ns = 1 so A is the Rabi rate
conventions.transmon: H_0 = (alpha/2) n (n-1) per qudit in its frame; coupling g (a^dag b + a b^dag), RWA
conventions.dissipation: T1: sqrt(1/T1) a; dephasing gamma_phi = 1/T2 - 1/(2 T1), jump sqrt(2 gamma_phi) n (coherence j,k decays at gamma_phi (j-k)^2)
conventions.ordering: qudit 0 is the least significant digit of the state index
conventions.clock: 2 GHz pulse clock: durations, sigma and drag beta in kernels are in clock cycles (2 per ns); beta_ns values here are converted by the tests

kinds.first_principles: exact diagonalization or exponentiation of a small matrix written from the Hamiltonian above in plain numpy
kinds.paper: number published in the cited paper (verified against arXiv text)

entries.citation: I. I. Rabi, Phys. Rev. 51, 652 (1937), doi:10.1103/PhysRev.51.652
entries.formula: P1 = sin^2(A T / 2)

entries.citation: Rabi (1937); e.g. Krantz et al., Appl. Phys. Rev. 6, 021318 (2019), arXiv:1904.06560
entries.formula: P1 = (A/W)^2 sin^2(W T / 2), W = sqrt(A^2 + delta^2), delta = w_tone - w_q
entries.note: insensitive to the sign of delta; pair with ef_rabi_sign for the sign

entries.citation: transmon level structure: Koch et al., PRA 76, 042319 (2007), arXiv:cond-mat/0703002
entries.formula: from |1>, tone at w_q + alpha drives 1-2 resonantly: P2 ~ sin^2(sqrt(2) A T / 2)
first order: leakage from |1> ~ |1 + beta alpha|^2 -> beta* = -1/alpha; phase-error optimum near -1/(2 alpha)

params.envelope: E = G(t) + i beta dG/dt, G truncated (not lifted) Gaussian

entries.note: a 4-sigma window (8 ns) moves the leakage minimum to beta ~ -0.1 ns: edge truncation dominates; use >= 8 sigma
